flags.name: cache-dump
flags.usage: print what the cache table for this project holds, and exit

flags.name: coverage
flags.usage: name every rule once under the coverage fact that describes it, rather than only counting them

flags.name: directory
flags.usage: the project root, which every relative path resolves against (default: the directory of the nearest tsconfig.json or Package.swift at or above the working directory)

flags.name: explain
flags.usage: report what every rule did on one file, and why it did or did not run

flags.name: fix
flags.usage: apply fixes only, running no other phase; add --format to format as well

flags.name: fix-passes
flags.usage: how many times a file may be re-linted while fixes keep landing

flags.name: format
flags.usage: format the files not on record as formatted, or the paths named; with --no-fix, report them instead

flags.name: format-all
flags.usage: format every file, not only the ones not on record as formatted (implies --format)

flags.name: lint
flags.usage: run the lint rules only, reporting their findings without fixing them and without TypeScript's diagnostics

flags.name: lint-config
flags.usage: the settings file that says which rules apply to which files, relative to --directory or else to where you typed it; unnamed, the file of this name at the project root

flags.name: no-cache
flags.usage: read nothing from and write nothing to this project's caches (the cache table and the tsconfig's incremental build info), so every phase computes from source

flags.name: no-fix
flags.usage: mutate no source in the checked project: report what would change without writing a byte of it (cohere still keeps its own cache in the project's .cache/cohere, unless --no-cache)

flags.name: print-config
flags.usage: print, as JSON in ESLint's --print-config shape, every registered rule's resolved severity and options for one file (the path given, else index.ts at the project root), and exit

flags.name: profile
flags.usage: write a Go CPU profile of the run to file, for go tool pprof

flags.name: rules
flags.usage: print the rules this cohere implements for the project's language, one per line, and exit

flags.name: rules-enabled
flags.usage: print the rules the lint config resolves for one file (the path given, else index.ts at the project root), with severity, and exit

flags.name: single-threaded
flags.usage: use one checker instead of several

flags.name: stdin-filepath
flags.usage: with --fix, read one file's text from stdin and print what --fix (and --format, if named) would write for the file at this path, writing nothing to disk

flags.name: timing
flags.usage: report what each rule cost, most expensive first

flags.name: tsconfig
flags.usage: the tsconfig that defines the program, relative to --directory or else to where you typed it; unnamed, the file of this name in --directory, or else the nearest one at or above the working directory

flags.name: types
flags.usage: report TypeScript's own diagnostics only, running no rules and writing no fixes

flags.name: unused
flags.usage: report code that was written and never used: unreferenced exports, and statements nothing can reach

flags.name: unused-all
flags.usage: list the unused findings already marked cohere-keep rather than only counting them (implies --unused)

flags.name: unused-deep
flags.usage: also compute the transitive closure of unused code and group it into islands (implies --unused)

flags.name: version
flags.usage: print the version, what this binary was built from, and the Swift contract it speaks, and exit

verbs.name: rename
verbs.summary: Renames a symbol everywhere the type graph says it is used. The position form is primary; a bare name is refused when it is ambiguous. Nothing is written without --write.

flags.name: directory
flags.usage: the working directory paths resolve against (default: the process's own)

flags.name: dry-run
flags.usage: print the plan and write nothing (the default; accepted so it can be stated explicitly)

flags.name: single-threaded
flags.usage: use one checker instead of several

flags.name: tsconfig
flags.usage: the tsconfig that defines the program, relative to --directory

flags.name: write
flags.usage: apply the rename; without it nothing is written
